One thing worth checking before this merges. AWS's own Python sample for this endpoint ([aws-samples/amazon-transcribe-streaming-python-websockets](https://github.com/aws-samples/amazon-transcribe-streaming-python-websockets/blob/main/example.py)) leaves `ping_interval` at the default but sets `ping_timeout=None`:

```python
async with websockets.connect(request_url,
                              extra_headers=extra_headers,
                              ping_timeout=None,
                              ) as websocket:
```

So pings are clearly accepted: the sample sends one every 20s, and `_verify_connection` in `websocket_service.py` already pings this endpoint on every reconnect. But AWS turned off the part that waits for the pong.

If the endpoint doesn't answer pings reliably, restoring the default `ping_timeout` would close healthy connections about 40s in, which is worse than the half-open case this fixes. I can't run it without AWS credentials. Could someone who has them stream a minute or two through this branch and confirm the connection survives past 40s?

Thanks for checking against the AWS sample. We don't have AWS credentials either, so we haven't streamed a live session through this branch; the test only covers a silent local socket. The concern is fair: the sample sets `ping_timeout=None`, so we can't tell whether the endpoint answers pings reliably. If someone with AWS access can stream 1-2 minutes and confirm the connection survives past 40s, that settles it. Otherwise we can keep the default `ping_interval` and set an explicit, larger `ping_timeout` (e.g. 60s) so half-open sockets still get detected. Happy to push that instead if you prefer.

Disclosure: this reply was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code) and has not been verified against a live AWS endpoint.

The second option sounds right to me: keep the default `ping_interval` and set an explicit `ping_timeout` of 60s. That still catches half-open sockets, and it doesn't depend on how quickly AWS answers pings. Someone with AWS access can confirm it later.

Pushed the second option: the connect call keeps the default `ping_interval` and now passes an explicit `ping_timeout=60` (a module constant, `KEEPALIVE_PING_TIMEOUT`). The half-open test still shortens the timings so it runs quickly, and now also asserts the service passes `ping_timeout=60` with no `ping_interval` override. As you said, it would still be good for someone with AWS access to confirm a live session later.

Disclosure: this change was made with AI assistance (Claude Code). The tests were run locally against a local websocket server only, not a live AWS endpoint.
